title: Partners
purpose: Every hour reaches the client through the same spine, whoever runs the floor, so a partner's site is as safe to sell as our own.
how: Two channels feed one spine. Direct operations: our team, about 135 phones, factories and warehouses. Delivery partners: Shedi, about 105 of our phones across hotels in four cities, fully independent; the Mansoura partner, about 30; franchise-style partners on their own sites. About 270 phones in all, and the client sees one company.

The spine is what every channel shares and none may skip. Onboarding screening for every wearer. One account per person, in their name, created by KMSC. Our review of every video before the client sees it. Pay on accepted hours net of fraud flags. A channel is how we reach a floor. The spine is what makes the hours worth buying.

Founders close every partnership. Adham owns the contract; Mano does the paperwork. Moharam runs the relationship day to day. Mano handles the money. Partners sit outside the org chart on purpose: their people are not KMSC staff, and they never contact the client.

One agreement, seven terms, the same for every partner. Pay on accepted hours net of fraud. The spine as a condition of payment. Our phones under MDM, with custody and return terms. Upload responsibility. Data-protection flow-downs. Audit rights. Exit within 7 days with a device count. Nobody edits a term in the field. A partner who wants a different deal is telling you something about the partnership.

Money moves for a partner the way it moves for us. The client pays on accepted hours after the month-end audit. A partner's hours are counted the same way, from the QC verdicts and the wearer log, with flagged footage off the top. Payment holds while a device count is open. Above the threshold, Adham signs second. Partner rates live in the agreement and nowhere else.

Which channel for a new site. We have the bench and the site has fiber or a hub in reach: direct. Someone already runs the floor and will take our phones and our spine: partner operator. Someone has sites and people and wants to deliver hours to our standard: delivery partner. In all three the gate is ours. Moharam certifies the site before an hour counts, and only when Mano confirms every wearer file and the quartermaster confirms the count.

procedures.name: Closing a partnership
steps: Walk the partner's floors. Count the phones needed, confirm the upload path, and name the task categories the sites add.
Sign the standard agreement. The seven terms are not edited in the field; Adham changes a term or nobody does.
Record payment terms with Mano. Name Moharam as the day-to-day contact on both sides.
No phone leaves the store until the agreement is signed and the first site has a plan.

procedures.name: Handing phones to a partner
steps: Enroll every phone before it leaves: Apple Business Manager, Hexnode, supervised, the collection app in kiosk, visible on the map.
Issue whole kits per ten phones with a manifest. Custody is signed at handover, and the partner becomes the custodian in the registry the same day.
Confirm the upload path in the site plan: the partner's own line, qualified at 100 Mbps sustained or better, or a hub run under our transport rules.
Run one 30-minute test session per phone on the partner's floor and confirm it uploads.

procedures.name: Onboarding a partner's wearer
procedures.owner: Mano owns the gate; Mazen runs it at the partner's Day 0; Moharam certifies
steps: The partner nominates. KMSC activates: ID copied, 18 or older, consent signed in Arabic and explained in person.
Fraud briefing delivered and signed off. One account, in the wearer's name, created by KMSC.
Enter the wearer in the log: name, device number, site, start date.
Rig fitted, angle checked, the first 30 minutes reviewed before the second 30 happen.
No paperwork, no account. No account, no hours.

procedures.name: Monthly partner settlement
steps: After the month-end audit, pull accepted hours per partner from the QC verdicts and the wearer log.
Take flagged footage off the top. Hours on a shared or unpapered account are zero.
Check the registry. No open device variance, or payment holds until the count matches.
Above the threshold, Adham signs second. Then pay, on the same cycle as site payments.

procedures.name: Partner audit
steps: Quarterly at partner premises, and any day Moharam asks. Count phones against the registry and the MDM.
Read the wearer log against the gate files. Every name has an ID copy, a consent form, and a fraud sign-off.
Walk the floor: angle on the heads, signage at the entrances, sensitive areas marked off.
Any variance is investigated the same day. Unexplained after 24 hours means lost mode, and Adham hears it that night.

procedures.name: A flag at a partner site
steps: Flag to Moharam and the partner the same day, with the session ID and the specific correction.
The partner corrects the wearer within 24 hours and tells Moharam it is done.
A second strike pauses the device until the wearer is retrained. Three flags pulls the wearer, never re-enrolled under any name or device.
Flagged hours come off the invoice and off the partner's payment, in that order.

procedures.name: Ending a partnership
procedures.owner: Adham decides; Moharam and Mano run the exit
steps: Notice in writing, either side, any reason. Ours goes out from Adham. Theirs comes to Moharam, who sends it to Adham and Mano the same day. The 7-day clock starts the day the notice is received.
Every phone is flushed before it travels. Every phone, mount, and charger is back within 7 days and counted against the registry.
Close every account. Nothing is recycled. Take the wearer log.
Payment releases when the count matches. A phone not back on day 7 goes into lost mode that day: 24 hours to recover, then wipe, police report, and a registry update.

breaks.what: A partner's wearer filmed without passing the gate
breaks.do: The device comes off them now; Moharam confirms it the same hour. Youssef Medhat holds every session from that device, unsent. Mano is told the same day. Those hours are not paid. Moharam re-checks every wearer on that site before filming resumes.

breaks.what: A partner site holds more than one device-day of footage
breaks.do: It is an incident, the same as on our own sites. Moharam the same day. The partner drains tonight on their own line; that is their term. If the line cannot, our runner takes a third of the phones per run to the nearest hub under the transport rules, or Mano fixes the line. Phones do not sleep full on anyone's premises.
Payment holds until the count is done. It is in the agreement for exactly this moment. Moharam tells Adham the same day.

breaks.what: A partner stops answering, or walks with devices
breaks.do: MDM locate first. Lost mode within the hour. 24 hours to recover, then wipe, police report, and a registry update. Payments hold. Adham hears it the same night, and the 7-day exit clock starts.

breaks.what: Accounts shared between a partner's wearers
breaks.do: Every hour on the shared account is unpaid, and the account closes. The partner re-gates every wearer on that site before filming resumes. A second time, Adham decides whether the partnership continues.

breaks.what: A partner or their worker names or contacts the client
breaks.do: Moharam has filming paused at that site within the hour. Adham handles everything client-facing. The agreement calls it a breach, and Adham decides the same day whether the partnership survives it.

breaks.what: A phone with footage on it is lost at a partner site, or a clip leaks
breaks.do: Moharam and Mano within the hour, and Mano brings counsel. Lost mode on the phone within the hour. Adham calls the client inside 24 hours and Mano with counsel notifies the regulator inside 72, so the partner's clock to us is the hour, not the day. It says so in the agreement.

breaks.what: A partner disputes the accepted-hours count
breaks.do: Moharam for the facts, Mano for the money, Adham for the contract, the same day. The record is the QC verdicts and the wearer log, and the month-end audit is final. Payment holds while any device count is open. Nobody, including us, is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

training: Moharam and Mano: the seven terms and what each one is for, one afternoon with Adham, before their first partner conversation.
Partner floor leads: the anchor day-one module, two hours, from Mazen at their first Day 0. Rig, angle, the 30-minute cycle, hat off means tap stop, custody.
Partner wearers: the same fraud briefing as ours, in Arabic, in person, signed off before the first shift.
Quartermaster: the partner handover, the manifest, and custody, inside the one-day training with Mano.

questions.q: Why put our phones on a partner's floor instead of using theirs?
questions.a: Because the phone is the control. MDM, kiosk, the map, the wipe. On their phones we would have their word. On ours we have the count.

questions.q: A partner already has trained people. Do they still go through the gate?
questions.a: Yes. Every wearer, every channel. ID, consent, briefing, one account, the log. Trained is not the same as papered.

questions.q: What does a partner get paid?
questions.a: It is in their agreement and nowhere else. Not on this site, not in a chat. The shape is public: accepted hours, net of fraud flags, after the audit.

questions.q: Can a partner talk to the client?
questions.a: Never. Not their owner, not their floor lead, not a wearer. Anything client-facing goes to Moharam, then Adham.

questions.q: Shedi is fully independent. What does that mean?
questions.a: They run their own floors, their own people, and their own uploads on the hotels' lines. They do not run their own gate, their own accounts, their own review, or their own count. That is the spine, and it is ours.

partners.name: Direct operations
partners.model: KMSC staff on KMSC phones, the whole spine in-house

partners.name: Mansoura partner
partners.model: Their floor, our phones, the standard agreement

partners.name: Delivery partners
partners.model: Their sites, their people, our phones and our standards; phones set per site at central planning

agreement.term: Pay on accepted hours net of fraud
agreement.text: The partner is paid for hours the client accepts, after the month-end audit, with flagged footage taken off first. The same way we are paid. Nobody is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

agreement.term: The spine as a condition of payment
agreement.text: Every wearer through the gate: ID copied, 18 or older, consent signed, fraud briefing signed off, one account in their name, entered in the wearer log. Every video through our review. Hours on an unpapered or shared account are zero.

agreement.term: Our phones under MDM, with custody and return terms
agreement.text: The phones are Vound assets on the partner's premises. Enrolled and supervised, the collection app in kiosk, on the map at all times. Custody signed at handover and at every transfer. Phones live at the site, at a hub, or in a signed-for case. Never at anyone's home.

The partner gets footage off every phone every day. Their own line, qualified at 100 Mbps sustained or better, or a hub run under our transport rules. Nothing sleeps holding more than one day of footage. A site holding more than one device-day is an incident.

The partner is bound as we are bound. Consent before filming, signage at the entrances, no filming in restrooms, locker rooms, prayer rooms, clinics, or offices. No uploads through anyone's home. A lost phone, a leaked clip, or a complaint reaches Moharam and Mano within the hour, so Adham can meet our 24-hour clock to the client.

We count phones, read the wearer log, check the gate files, and walk the floor at partner premises. Quarterly by the calendar, and any day Moharam asks. A refused audit holds payment until the count is done.

agreement.term: Exit within 7 days with a device count
agreement.text: Either side may end it, in writing, for any reason. Within 7 days every phone, mount, and charger is back and counted against the registry. Accounts close and are never recycled. Payment releases when the count matches.
